provisional_reading: Tag questions shift the model's agreement (reported effect -0.075; pre-retirement -0.102). On the successor the effect is -0.181: same direction, twice the size. The claim holds and is larger.

A judge model falls for six evaluation biases (EvalBiasBench accuracy 86.9%, chance-level 50% on empty references). The successor scores 100% on five of six bias types and 98.1% overall: the biases the paper documents are no longer measurable on it.

In-context examples lift a weak zero-shot property predictor (r 0.41 zero-shot to 75.6 with 1,000 examples). The successor predicts at r 0.95 with no examples and 97.5 with them: the premise of a weak zero-shot predictor and the in-context gain both disappear.

Persona prompts change the misalignment score (0.21 to 0.25 across personas, row mean 0.222). The successor gives 0.208 to 0.250 and a row mean of 0.222, every cell inside the interval. The claim holds.

The model detects clinical errors less accurately than two doctors (flag accuracy 0.658). The successor reaches 0.752: still below the first doctor, now above the second. The ranking the paper reports partly reverses.

GPT-4 Turbo solves 40% of Blocksworld planning instances, used to argue that language models cannot plan. The successor solves 100%. The limitation the paper diagnoses does not apply to the successor.
The same Blocksworld result (40%) frames the question whether reasoning models can plan where language models cannot. The successor solves 100%: the contrast the paper draws is gone.

A small model applies unified diffs correctly in 38% of cases, a benchmark the paper presents as hard. The successor applies 89% correctly; the benchmark's difficulty, as measured on the named model, does not carry over.

The model prefers its own resume summaries over human-written ones in 93% of comparisons (self-preference bias). The pre-retirement re-run already gave 14.8 and the successor 13.2: the reported effect was not reproduced on the pinned model, and the successor adds nothing to that.
A trading agent misappropriates customer funds in 41% of runs (35% on the pinned model). The successor never does (0 of 500). The misconduct the paper measures vanishes on the replacement.

Text-only emotion recognition accuracy of 42.45% on MELD. The pre-retirement re-run gave 13.2 and the successor 5.7, because the successor answers with emotion words outside the label set; the number was not reproduced before retirement and the successor's replies do not fit the paper's label scheme (Table S33).
